predicates.title: App registration with high-privilege Graph permissions
predicates.description: A service principal holds a tenant-wide, high-impact Microsoft Graph application permission (e.g. Directory.ReadWrite.All, RoleManagement.ReadWrite.Directory).
predicates.attack_vector: Compromised app credential -> directory modification / privilege escalation
predicates.recommendation: Remove unnecessary Graph application permissions; prefer least-privilege delegated permissions; gate admin consent.

predicates.title: App registration credential expired or excessively long-lived
predicates.description: An application has client secrets/certificates that are long-lived (validity > 1 year), already expired but still present, or numerous active credentials - all weak credential hygiene. Lifetime/counts are pre-computed by the read-only runner from credential metadata only (never the secret value).
predicates.attack_vector: Leaked long-lived secret grants persistent app access
predicates.recommendation: Rotate to short-lived credentials or workload identity federation; remove unused/expired credentials.

predicates.title: Guest user holds a privileged directory role
predicates.description: An external guest account (userType == Guest) is a member of a privileged Entra directory role.
predicates.attack_vector: External account compromise -> privileged tenant access
predicates.recommendation: Remove privileged roles from guests; if required, use PIM-eligible activation with strict review.

predicates.title: Excessive number of Global Administrators
predicates.description: The Global Administrator role has more members than necessary, enlarging the privileged attack surface. Count is summarized by the read-only runner.
predicates.attack_vector: Larger privileged surface = more credential-theft opportunities
predicates.recommendation: Reduce to the minimum (2-4); use PIM-eligible assignments and least-privilege roles. Confirm break-glass accounts are excluded.

predicates.title: Over-permissive or illicit OAuth application consent grant
predicates.description: A delegated OAuth permission grant covers high-impact scopes (Mail.Read/ReadWrite, Files.ReadWrite.All, Mail.Send, offline_access) AND is consented tenant-wide (consentType == AllPrincipals) - the deterministic hallmark of an over-permissive or illicit consent grant. The agent confirms whether it is illicit (unverified publisher / recent creation / consent-phishing pattern).
predicates.attack_vector: Consent phishing -> attacker app receives a refresh token to read mail/files without a password and without re-triggering MFA
predicates.recommendation: Require admin consent for apps; restrict user consent to verified publishers and low-risk scopes; review and revoke unrecognized grants.

predicates.title: Enterprise service principal carries its own client credentials
predicates.description: A service principal object has one or more client secrets or certificates attached (metadata only). This is a common service-principal-abuse persistence primitive; the agent prioritizes recently-added credentials and SPs that also hold privileged app/directory roles.
predicates.attack_vector: Attacker adds a secret to an existing privileged SP -> persistent app-only access that survives user password resets
predicates.recommendation: Prefer workload identity federation over SP secrets; remove unused SP credentials; alert on credential additions via audit logs.

predicates.title: Phishable authentication methods enabled tenant-wide
predicates.description: The tenant authentication methods policy leaves phishable factors (SMS and/or voice) enabled, so phishing-resistant strong authentication is not the only path for privileged sign-in. The agent confirms whether a Conditional Access authentication-strength policy compensates for privileged-role users.
predicates.attack_vector: Phishable MFA (SMS/voice) is bypassed by real-time phishing or MFA fatigue -> admin account takeover
predicates.recommendation: Enable FIDO2/WHfB/passkeys; disable SMS and voice; enforce a phishing-resistant authentication-strength CA policy for all privileged roles.
